scope: Four visual concepts for the scrolling 3D website based on poster 01; static concept mockups, not implemented websites.

variants.name: The living diagram

design.type: Distinctive rounded geometric grotesk headings; humanist sans body; sentence case.
design.layout: Asymmetric editorial zigzag: text left / scene right, then scene left / text right, on one uninterrupted light canvas.
design.signature: One sculptural jade return cable connects the complete sequence across generous open space.

variants.direction:
DIRECTION A — THE LIVING DIAGRAM. A warm, airy editorial workshop: an elevated dimensional translation of the original poster's personality. Use a porcelain-ivory canvas, vivid cobalt enamel machines, amber acrylic token tiles, jade rubber return tubing, and occasional brushed aluminum details. Sophisticated studio product rendering, soft daylight, exquisite contact shadows, subtly bevelled real 3D forms, no drawn outlines or paper-print distress.
Layout: a very slim top navigation, then a compact left-aligned headline and a large hero diorama to its right. Continue downward through three broad alternating editorial compositions. Large 3D clusters extend freely into the whitespace, with balanced text columns alongside; do not box scenes into cards. The first cluster combines the laptop and open harness drawers with a few suspended context sheets. A slender orange transport path leads to a compact tunnel and then a large cobalt model engine, shown open so prefill/decode and green cache blocks are distinct. Below, a proposal receipt arrives at the policy gate before a file-and-test workshop; a beautiful continuous jade cable curls back upward along the outer margin to the harness. Finish with a small verified-diff object beside the final reading beat.
Make the page unmistakably modern web editorial: restrained medium-sized geometric display type, mixed-case headings, quiet body text, generous 96px-like gutters. The hero and lower scenes should feel physically present and irresistibly tactile. Warm, approachable, clean, playful precision. No tan newspaper aesthetic. No oversize black all-caps poster title.
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one exceptionally polished, high-fidelity full-page DESKTOP WEBSITE screenshot for an educational 3D scrolling experience based on the supplied first poster. This is a new website concept, not an edit of the poster. Image 1 is a CONTENT and OBJECT-VOCABULARY reference: reinterpret its laptop, harness cabinet, encrypted request tunnel, model engine, amber tokens, policy gate, files, tests and return loop as beautifully rendered volumetric 3D objects.
Output one tall continuous webpage, approximately 1:2 portrait aspect ratio (ideally 1536 x 3072), viewed straight-on with flat, sharp web typography and convincingly dimensional 3D scenes. Desktop-width composition throughout, not a mobile app. Show the whole scroll journey in a carefully art-directed long page. Do not make a collage of browser windows, design boards, or multiple screenshots.
The page should feel like a distinctive premium interactive learning experience: a visitor scrolls, the camera travels between connected 3D scenes, parts open or separate to reveal their function, and readable editorial copy alternates with those scenes. Keep wide outer margins (roughly 8% of the page), generous breathing room and clear readable type. Main title compact, not a giant poster banner. Use only a few words per line in headings and comfortable short paragraphs. Most objects should be large enough to understand immediately. Put technical details in the explanations, not a cloud of floating micro-labels. A quiet chapter/progress control and a small 'Scroll to explore' affordance establish the website interaction.
Semantic sequence, mandatory: user request -> harness assembles context -> JSON over encrypted connection -> provider/token IDs -> model prefill and decode -> streamed proposal returns to harness -> policy check -> tools act -> tool results feed the next model turn and verification. Never draw model directly executing tools. Never suggest one input token equals one output token. Clearly distinguish proposing from acting.
Use the following exact, correctly spelled website copy, with line breaks chosen to fit:
Main title: "How a coding agent works"
Opening sentence: "Scroll through one request."
Request shown near the laptop: "Fix the race condition in the job scheduler."
First reading beat: "Build the request"
"The harness gathers instructions, tools, environment and conversation."
Second reading beat: "Run the model"
"Text becomes token IDs. Prefill reads the prompt; decode generates the response."
Third reading beat: "The model proposes. The harness acts."
"The harness checks policy before tools edit files and run tests."
Final reading beat: "Return. Repair. Verify."
"Tool results return as context. Repeat, retest and summarize."
Useful short object labels, only where clear: "Harness", "JSON", "Model", "Prefill", "Decode", "KV cache", "Policy", "Tools", "Results".
Navigation can say "Agent loop", "Explore", "Chapters". No unrelated branding, pricing, testimonials, marketing claims, source-document mentions, credits, page footers or watermarks. No giant rounded-card grid, no infographic speech bubbles, no hand-drawn outlines, no wall of arrows. Keep text separate from complex objects and shadows. This must look like a beautiful usable WEBSITE, not a flat infographic pasted into a webpage. Design for an adult audience: playful, intelligent, clean and tactile.

variants.name: Inside the engine

design.type: Confident wide contemporary sans headings with clear, quieter humanist body.
design.layout: Full-bleed cinematic scenes dissolve into one continuous cobalt environment; concise copy occupies deliberate calm pockets.
design.signature: The visitor follows a luminous amber token through a monumental working machine.

variants.direction:
DIRECTION B — INSIDE THE ENGINE. A cinematic immersive scroll journey through one monumental blue machine. Use a rich deep ultramarine environment, vivid electric-cobalt coated metal, milky glass interfaces, elegant silver structural edges, honey-amber token light, and restrained jade feedback paths. It must feel expensive, vivid and calm, not a black-and-neon cyberpunk HUD or outer-space game.
Layout: full-bleed continuous 3D environment with three or four deliberate open reading zones, generous safe margins, bright ice-white flat web text. Start with the compact title at upper left and a striking close 3D view of a laptop/request capsule entering a cobalt harness. As the page descends the camera appears to push past the encrypted request conduit into the model's open architectural core. Show prefill/decode as distinct nested mechanical volumes, green KV blocks, and a measured trail of amber token tiles. Continue into a lower scene where the output becomes a proposal scroll, then encounters a jade policy iris before reaching the file/test tools. A jade return channel travels back toward the harness.
Compose with tremendous depth, controlled reflections, soft volumetric light and precise focus on the object silhouettes; no bloom over the text. Let the perspective and scale change between scroll chapters, while the whole page remains visually continuous. Each of the required copy blocks has a quiet dark-blue negative-space zone next to its scene, never on top of busy machinery. Thin restrained progress marks at the far right. An exciting immersive web experience with educational clarity, generous whitespace inside a dark palette, and no floating dashboard card clutter.

variants.name: The token playground

design.type: Friendly substantial rounded sans headings; highly legible softer sans body.
design.layout: A winding vertical path of floating sculptural workstations, interleaved with spacious alternating text bays.
design.signature: A token-sized point of view travels between miniature islands connected by sculptural cables.

variants.direction:
DIRECTION C — THE TOKEN PLAYGROUND. A joyful, extremely clean spatial learning world with floating miniature workstations on a luminous pale-sky backdrop. Think collectible industrial-design toys, smooth colored porcelain and satin plastic, beautiful soft global illumination. Cobalt machines, marigold tokens, mint feedback pipes, white platforms, navy text. Adult sophistication and a tiny touch of wonder; no cartoon faces, mascots, scenery filler, confetti, planets or clouds of decorative particles.
Layout: a calm left-aligned web header and compact friendly title, then one continuous winding journey diagonally across and down the page. Large sculptural station clusters sit on a few white floating plinths, linked by deliberate slender orange forward tracks and a clearly separate mint return track. The request laptop and harness are the first station; the encrypted conduit and provider entrance bridge to the open model island; the proposal receipt, policy checkpoint and tool workshop form the lower station. A final small diff sheet stands beside the final copy. Make the stages recognizable from the source, reimagined as inviting high-quality physical objects.
Alternate generous text bays with the islands so the site breathes. Use large empty sky areas as functional margins and transition space. A small persistent path progress widget suggests that scrolling flies the camera from one station to the next. The reader should feel they could drag to orbit each machine or tap a token. Lovely playful curves, carefully aligned text, crisp realistic volumetric shadows, no black cartoon outlines, no infographic bubbles, no tiny dense technical labels. Keep the whole request, computation, policy, action and feedback loop visually intelligible.

variants.name: The exploded-view studio

design.type: Precise contemporary neo-grotesk; medium-weight display and calm regular body.
design.layout: A generous left reading column and a dominant right 3D stage, with successive exploded states connected vertically.
design.signature: A translucent modular system opens layer by layer as the user scrolls; the text controls attention.

variants.direction:
DIRECTION D — THE EXPLODED-VIEW STUDIO. A bright, ultra-refined interactive product-explainer website built around an exploded physical model of the agent system. White and pale cool-gray background, crystal-clear acrylic, satin aluminum, royal-blue enamel structural components, amber token tiles, emerald permission and feedback accents. Photorealistic industrial design visualization, beautiful refraction, soft shadows and precise component edges. Clean, inviting and quietly playful when the parts lift and open; not a blueprint or dense developer dashboard.
Layout: a strong asymmetrical split screen, roughly 34% editorial reading column and 66% large open 3D canvas. Use one continuous full-length web page showing the scroll-linked transformations of the same coherent system. The top has a slim quiet navigation and a compact headline in the reading column while the complete device floats beautifully on the right. Lower down, the assembly opens: context sheets and harness drawers separate, then a transparent encrypted transport conduit reveals amber request tokens, then the model chassis lifts to reveal clearly separated prefill, decode and green KV-cache pieces. The lowest view exposes a distinct policy latch between the proposal and the file/test mechanism, with a looping emerald return channel. A few clear short component labels appear only on physical parts.
Place the required editorial beats in the left column at the matching vertical points; let the last paragraph open into a full-width quiet finishing area beside a small verified diff object. Fine alignment, ample 100px-like margins, airy 40–60-character body lines, restrained mixed-case typography, meaningful hairlines only where needed. The focus is a beautifully engineered physical system whose internals become understandable as it opens. No rounded UI card grid, no fake code, no huge headline, no gratuitous wireframes or measurement clutter.

refinements.prompt:
Make a precise localized correction to this finished 3D WEBSITE design. Preserve its cinematic cobalt and chrome environment, all typography, composition, dimensions, lighting, objects and copy. Correct ONLY the emerald feedback conduit so it clearly carries tool RESULTS back to the HARNESS, never into the provider.
At the bottom, the green conduit must leave the Tools/Tests area, pass the 'Results' label, then flow RIGHT along the bottom and UP the right edge. Reverse the mistaken left-pointing arrows along the bottom to point right. At the TOP, extend the return conduit leftwards BEHIND the Provider cabinet until it joins the SIDE OF THE HARNESS cabinet (the cabinet beside the laptop). It must not enter the Provider cabinet. Show the final small arrow entering the harness. Keep this upper bend in the scene's open background, with no overlap on any heading or paragraph. Maintain all other forward paths and the model-proposal-policy-tools sequence exactly. Do not add any new labels, features, footer, credit or watermark. Output the full finished tall webpage.

Refine this completed floating-workstation 3D WEBSITE with two precise corrections. Preserve all existing style, sky color, objects, page layout, typography, headings, copy and whitespace except these targeted details.
1. Replace the literal fake code on the Proposal sheet with clean schematic blue-gray text strokes and a short readable 'edit_file' label. Keep its 'Proposal' title. On the final 'Verified patch' sheet replace its literal fake code with simple red/green diff strokes and plus/minus marks, with NO code words. Keep its heading. Do not invent executable example code.
2. Correct the mint feedback conduit. It must start from the Tools workstation, feed the Results screen, then continue UP THE FAR LEFT OUTER MARGIN all the way to the upper Harness cabinet, ending in an arrow entering the harness side. It must NOT end at or enter the Proposal sheet. Extend the current left-side green run upward to the harness, keeping it clear of the main title, laptop screen and all text. Keep the Proposal sheet's incoming and outgoing AMBER path intact. Remove the incorrect green branch that leads into the final Verified patch sheet; that final sheet is a clean standalone final artifact, not a conduit endpoint. The feedback path should read Tools -> Results -> Harness. Keep every other pixel and all other words as close as possible. No footer, new text or watermark. Output the complete tall webpage.

Make a precise cleanup of the LOWEST feedback illustration in this finished bright 3D WEBSITE. Preserve the complete design, typography, layout, colors, all upper scenes, and the four left-column reading beats.
Fix the green feedback conduit at the bottom so the flow is Tools -> Results -> Harness. The vertical green conduit at the lower-right must LEAVE the upper Tools cabinet and point DOWN, then curve left along the back of the lowest scene into the Results object at lower left. A short distinct green connection must then lead RIGHT from Results into the lower Harness cabinet. No green arrow should point up into Tools. Remove the decorative self-loop in front of the lower Harness, so the path is simple and readable. Keep the 'Verified patch' sheet beside the lower harness but remove its literal 'edit_file' fake code; use only red/green schematic diff strokes and plus/minus marks beneath its heading. The verified sheet is standalone, not an endpoint of a green pipe. Keep all other scene details and all copy unchanged. No new labels, new footers, credits or watermarks. Output the entire tall webpage.

Edit only the two short connections around the Results screen near the bottom of this completed sky-blue 3D website design. Keep the whole page and every word unchanged. The Tools workstation at lower right must visibly connect to the Results screen at lower left: add one short neat mint-green conduit from the underside of Tools, descending slightly and then running LEFT into the RIGHT edge of the Results screen. Put ONE left-pointing arrow on this short incoming conduit. Keep it in the empty gap immediately below the Tools platform, well above the Verified patch sheet and the final paragraph. On the LEFT side of the Results screen, REMOVE the existing large right-pointing arrowhead that points into Results. Replace that arrowhead with a plain smooth pipe join, keeping the existing small left-pointing chevrons and the long upward return pipe unchanged. This gives one coherent path: Tools -> Results -> upward return pipe -> Harness. No pipe should touch the Proposal sheet or Verified patch sheet. Do not change any other part of the image. Output the entire tall finished website design.
